links.effect: In an ablation on 25 cases, 166 deterministic post-processing rules improved binary check pass rate by 11.7 percentage points and eliminated all 6 fabrication-class failures.
links.quote: We initially deployed 166 such rules across 6 profiles; in a controlled ablation on 25 cases (  n = 25, drawn from the multi-site case pool), these rules improved binary check pass rate by 11.7 per-centage points and eliminated all 6 fabrication-class failures.

links.outcome: Regressions after verified updates to production documentation agents
links.effect: Closed-loop verification resolved physician complaints with zero regressions on 42 tracked cases across 1,089 optimization iterations; unverified prompt optimization of an assembly agent produced 18–28 point regressions.
links.quote: A closed-loop quality system deployed across thirteen US hospital sites resolved physician complaints with zero regressions on 42 tracked cases across 1,089 optimization iterations, while a deterministic assembly-agent replacement cut H+P trace latency from 19.6 s to 10.8 s (−8.8 s, 95% CI [−10.5, −7.1] s;  n = 100 pre,  n = 100 post).

links.outcome: Inter-rater agreement among physician raters of note preference
links.effect: Cohen's κ = 0.028 (95% CI −0.30 to 0.36) between two board-certified emergency physicians on 35 overlapping pairs; consistent with no agreement above chance.
links.quote: Third, a calibration study expanding from one physician rater to three (  n = 84 ratings across 36 blind pairs) found that the physician-preference signal is rater-fragile at this sample size: between two board-certified emergency physicians, Cohen’s  κ = 0.028 with 95% CI [−0.30, 0.36] on  n = 35 overlapping pairs.
